newsitem.title: INDIA: India taxes clearing agents, forwarders, rental cars.
newsitem.headline: India taxes clearing agents, forwarders, rental cars.

text.p: The Indian government on Friday decided to impose a five percent service tax on clearing and forwarding agents, and rental car operators beginning July 16, an official statement said.
Finance Minister P. Chidambaram had indicated when he unveiled the 1997/98 (April-March) budget in February that a service tax would be levied on various service sectors.

"The rate of tax is 5.0 percent and the tax will be computed on the gross amount of remuneration or commission paid to the clearing and forwarding agent by the principal engaging such an agent," the statement said.
The service tax on car rental operators will be levied on those who hold a licence under the rent-cab-scheme.
"The service tax will be at the rate of 5.0 percent on the gross amount charged to the customer for services in relation to the renting of a cab," the statement said.
